title: A Citation-Grounded Benchmark for Trustworthy Earnings Call Transcript Analysis with Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.00969v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly used for financial document analysis, including earnings call transcripts (ECTs). Beyond generating standalone claims, users increasingly prefer grounded analyses that pair claims with verifiable citations from source documents to enable independent validation. However, evaluating such analytical claims typically requires extensive expert annotation, which is costly and difficult to scale, and real-world financial analysis commonly involves long context-question-answer triplets, further increasing task complexity. To address these challenges and benchmark the current landscape of grounded analysis by LLMs, we propose a numeric evidence evaluation method that enables groundedness assessment without reliance on expert annotation. translated_title: 基于引用支撑的大语言模型可信盈利电话会议记录分析基准
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）在金融文档分析（包括盈利电话会议记录）中的应用日益增多。除了生成独立的论断之外，用户越来越倾向于有据可依的分析，即论断与源文档中可验证的引用相配对，以实现独立验证。然而，评估此类分析性论断通常需要大量的专家标注，成本高昂且难以规模化，而现实世界的金融分析通常涉及长上下文-问题-答案三元组，进一步增加了任务的复杂性。为了应对这些挑战并对大语言模型有据分析的现状进行基准测试，我们提出了一种数值证据评估方法，能够在不依赖专家标注的情况下评估论断的引用支撑性。我们还引入了一个自动化数据集构建流水线，并基于标普500指数前100大成分股构建了ECTs-100数据集，以支持对有据分析的基准测试……
tldr: 该论文提出了一种无需专家标注即可评估大语言模型论断引用支撑性的数值证据评估方法，并配合自动化数据集构建流水线，基于标普500前100大成分股构建了ECTs-100基准数据集，用于评估大语言模型在盈利电话会议记录分析中的可信度。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a numeric evidence evaluation method that enables groundedness assessment without expert annotation, and introduces ECTs-100, a benchmark dataset built from the top 100 S&P 500 constituents, to evaluate the trustworthiness of citation-grounded LLM analysis of earnings call transcripts.
